1. (1) This Ordinance may be cited as the Financial
Procedure Ordinance, 1957! and shall come into force
on such date as the Yang di-Pertuan Agong shall, by
notification in the Gazerte,! appoint and the Yang di-

coming into force of different provisions of this Ordi-
nance in different parts of the Federation.

(2) This Ordinance shall not apply to the Railway
Administration established under the provisions of the
Railway: Ordinance, 1948, ‘nor to any person in the
service of that Administration.                              .

2. Subject to thie provisions of Clause (4) of Article
165 of the Constitution, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong
may by notification in the Gazette, appoint a date, not
later than the date specified in Clause (1) of that Article,
for the coming into operation of Part VII of ne Consti-
tution.

3. In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise
requires—

"accounting officer" includes every public officer who
is charged with the duty of collecting, receiving, or
accounting for, or who in fact collects, receives or
accounts for, any public moneys, or who is charged with
the duty of disbursing, or who does in fact disburse,
any public moneys, and every public officer who is

PART | III

CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT OF PUBLIC FINANCES
OF THE FEDERATION

6. The Minister shall, subject to the provisions of the
Constitution and of this Ordinance, have the manage-
ment of the Consolidated Hund and the supervision,
control and direction of all matters relating to the
financial affairs of the Federation which are not as-
signed to any other Minister by any other law.

7. There shall be maintaimed by the Treasury in
respect of the Consolidated Fund three separate
accounts—

(a) an account to be called the Consolidated
Revenue Account in| which account shall be
kept of all moneys in the Fund other than
such moneys as are mentioned in paragraphs
(6) and (c);

(b) an account to be called the Consolidated Loan
Account in which account shall be kept of
all moneys received by way of loan upon the
public credit of the Federation; and

(c) an account to be called the Consolidated Trust
Account in which account shall be kept of
all moneys received subject to a trust and to
be applied in accordance with the terms of
the trust.
